answer: Quorum disagreement is a rule where a split verdict summons a second panel. Each validator must stake ivory bonds before voting, and the protocol locks those bonds until panels agree. A forger must stake once per identity per panel, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes plus a second round. Honest clusters converge on one marble tally, while farms fracture across many keys and cannot fake agreement cheaply. Repeated disagreement burns the staked ivory and the defence prices fakes past the horizon of profit.
